description:
Desktop client for openHPSDR Protocol 1/2 SDR radios.

A Rust/egui desktop client for openHPSDR Protocol 1 and Protocol 2 radios (Metis/Ozy-style and Hermes/Orion-style boards), using WDSP for DSP.

- Protocol 1 (Metis/Ozy) and Protocol 2 (Hermes/Orion) support, with standard openHPSDR UDP discovery
- Multiple simultaneous receivers, each with its own VFO, mode, filter width, and band memory
- Spectrum/waterfall display with adjustable dB range, palette, and Click-to-Tune (CTUN)
- SSB/CW/AM/FM/digital modes, per-mode/per-band filter width and mode memory
- Noise blanker (NB/NB2), noise reduction (NR/NR2/NNR), and SNB, independently switchable
- AGC with selectable Off/Long/Slow/Medium/Fast modes
- TX: mic audio through WDSP's TXA chain, ALC, TX power/SWR meter with per-band PA calibration, and a Tune button
- PureSignal (PA linearization/predistortion), on both Protocol 1 and Protocol 2
- rigctl (Hamlib-compatible), TCI (WebSocket), and CAT (Kenwood TS-2000 emulation) control servers
- Dual VFO (VFO A/B) with Split -- transmit on VFO B while receiving on VFO A
- Selectable RX output / TX input audio devices, independent of the OS default
- Per-radio settings persistence, keyed by the radio's MAC address
- FPGA firmware upload and static IP configuration
VFOs
- Click (or tap, on a touch screen) VFO-A or VFO-B to open the frequency keypad. It was right-click or a long press.
- Scroll over a digit of a VFO to step that digit up or down, one per wheel notch. The digit under the mouse is underlined. In the main window and extra receivers.
- Scrolling the spectrum or waterfall now moves by the VFO step (beside VFO-A), landing on multiples of it, as the controller's VFO knob does. Shift (100 Hz, 10 Hz in CW), Alt (10 Hz) and Ctrl (10 kHz, 1 Hz in CW) keep their fixed steps. MIDI VFO Step Up/Down use the VFO step too.
- The window size popup shown while resizing is gone.
Receive-only radios
- An RTL-SDR, MSI.SDR, RX-888, or a Pluto on its wide stream can no longer be put into transmit from a controller, MIDI, CAT, TCI or a serial PTT line (its MOX button was already hidden). TCI tells clients receive_only:true for these.
Linux / Raspberry Pi audio
- (System Default) now plays and records through PipeWire or PulseAudio (ALSA's pipewire or pulse device) when there is one, so hpsdr-rs appears in pavucontrol and follows the output you choose there. If neither will open, it uses ALSA's own default as before.
- If PipeWire is running but ALSA can't reach it, Settings → Audio says so: install pipewire-alsa (sudo apt install pipewire-alsa) and restart. Without it, a Raspberry Pi's default is the bcm2835 headphone jack, so a USB headset or HDMI monitor stays silent.
- hpsdr-remote does the same for its default output and mic, with the warning on its status line.
- The audio output reopens itself if ALSA leaves it dead after a "POLLERR" error, instead of staying silent.
Documentation
- Manual: "No sound on Linux or a Raspberry Pi" in Settings: Audio; the manual PDF builds again.
- README features rewritten, and a project website: https://g0orx.github.io/hpsdr-rs/
